title: Derivative under last-coordinate restriction
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$, let $i$ be a coordinate in $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $b$ be a bit, and let $x\in\{0,1\}^n$. The discrete derivative in direction $i$ of the restriction of $f$ to last coordinate $b$, evaluated at $x$, equals the discrete derivative of $f$ in coordinate $i$ at the point obtained by appending $b$ to $x$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the $(n+1)$-dimensional Boolean hypercube
replaced: Let $f:\{0,1\}^{n+1}\to\mathbb R$ and $f_b(x)=f(x,b)$. For $i<n$, $b\in\{0,1\}$, and $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, $D_i f_b(x)=D_i f(x,b)$, where $D_i$ is the coordinate half-difference.
